scenes.tts: Why would a polymer fall apart while its building blocks crowd around it? Watch one microtubule grow from a seed in purified tubulin. It lengthens slowly for minutes, then collapses many times faster. A crystal in its solution does not do this.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for the whole film: fresh-nucleotide subunits GOLD, old ADP/GDP subunits BLUE, tight end GREEN tag, loose end RED tag, free-subunit gauge TEAL, text TEXT. World: a dark field filled edge to edge with slowly drifting small gold dots (free tubulin), drifting for the whole film. From the first frame: a grey seed block at left-centre and a short tube (three parallel rows of blocks, gold at the tip and blue behind, about 1.2 units tall, in the middle band) pointing right, labelled 'microtubule, schematic'; a large '?' in TEXT sits above it. On 'Watch one microtubule' the tube starts extending right one block at a time at a steady slow pace; a small clock top-right labelled 'schematic' runs from 0:00 toward 3:00. Blocks join gold and turn blue a little behind the tip. On 'then collapses' the tube's right end splays into three outward-curling strands and the tube retreats toward the seed in about two seconds, many times faster than it grew; the gold dots keep drifting, as many as before. On 'A crystal' a gold cube slides in at the right edge among the same drifting dots; it neither grows nor shrinks, and a label 'crystal: settles' appears under it. The tube starts growing again slowly under the '?' as the sentence ends.
scenes.narration: Why would a polymer fall apart while its building blocks crowd around it? Watch one microtubule grow from a seed in purified tubulin. It lengthens slowly for minutes, then collapses many times faster. A crystal in its solution does not do this.

scenes.visual: Title card (TitleCard): LESSON 'Cytoskeletal Polymers and Dynamics', TITLE 'Tight Ends, Loose Ends'. The gold dots keep drifting behind it.

scenes.tts: Start with one end, and treat it as a doorway. Subunits arrive at a rate set by how many are free. They leave at a rate that does not depend on that. At one free concentration, the two balance. That is the end's critical concentration.
scenes.caption: Start with one end, and treat it as a doorway. Subunits arrive at a rate set by how many are free. They leave at a rate that does not depend on that. At one free concentration, the two balance. That is the end's critical concentration, Cc.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the tube's right end until it fills the left 60% of the frame height, drawn as a schematic row of blocks ending in an open doorway (two TEXT posts). Right side: a tall vertical TEAL gauge labelled 'free subunits' and 'schematic', with a sliding pointer. Above the doorway two arrows: an inward arrow labelled 'arrive' and an outward arrow labelled 'leave', each with a running tally counter (schematic). On 'treat it as a doorway' the posts draw on. On 'Subunits arrive' gold dots drift into the doorway and dock as blocks; the 'arrive' tally ticks. On 'how many are free' the gauge pointer rises, the dot field visibly thickens, the 'arrive' arrow thickens with it and docking speeds up. On 'They leave' blocks pop off the end at a steady beat and the 'leave' tally ticks. On 'does not depend' the pointer slides down and up again while the 'leave' arrow keeps exactly the same thickness and beat. On 'the two balance' the pointer settles where both arrows are equally thick and both tallies tick together. On 'critical concentration' a TEAL tick appears on the gauge at the pointer, labelled 'Cc'.
scenes.narration: Start with one end, and treat it as a doorway. Subunits arrive at a rate set by how many are free. They leave at a rate that does not depend on that. At one free concentration, the two balance. That is the end's critical concentration, Cc.

scenes.tts: Above it, the end grows. Below it, the end shrinks. If subunits never used their nucleotide, both ends would share one critical concentration. The polymer would grow until free subunits fell to that level, then simply settle.
scenes.visual: Same doorway and gauge. On 'Above it' the pointer rises above the Cc tick; the end gains blocks and a GREEN 'grows' arrow pushes right. On 'Below it' the pointer drops below Cc; blocks leave faster than they arrive, the end retreats, a RED 'shrinks' arrow points left. On 'never used their nucleotide' zoom out to the whole filament, every block one neutral colour (TEXT outline, no gold or blue), a doorway at each end. On 'share one critical concentration' each end gets an identical TEAL chip 'Cc', and the gauge keeps its single tick. On 'grow until' the pointer starts high, the filament lengthens at both ends while the pointer slides down to the single tick and the dot field thins. On 'simply settle' the length stops changing (a length bracket above it stops, labelled 'settled'); dots still drift and the tallies at each end still tick in step, showing exchange without net change.
scenes.narration: Above it, the end grows. Below it, the end shrinks. If subunits never used their nucleotide, both ends would share one critical concentration. The polymer would grow until free subunits fell to that level, then simply settle.

scenes.tts: Real actin and tubulin differ. Each subunit arrives carrying fresh A T P or G T P. Some time after joining, it hydrolyses that nucleotide and releases the phosphate. Those old subunits then hold on less tightly.
scenes.caption: Real actin and tubulin differ. Each subunit arrives carrying fresh ATP or GTP. Some time after joining, it hydrolyses that nucleotide and releases the phosphate. Those old subunits then hold on less tightly.
scenes.visual: Same filament, same place. On 'actin and tubulin differ' the 'settled' bracket fades and the neutral blocks start to recolour. On 'arrives carrying fresh' the free dots turn GOLD and a GOLD chip 'fresh: ATP or GTP' appears top-left; gold dots dock at the end as gold blocks. On 'after joining' a slow wave runs along the filament behind the newest blocks: after a visible delay, each block turns from GOLD to BLUE, so a gold tip trails into a blue body; a BLUE chip 'old: ADP or GDP' appears under the first chip. On 'hold on less tightly' thin schematic attachment marks between blue blocks fade slightly and the blue blocks wobble, while gold blocks stay snug. The wave keeps running so the picture never freezes.
scenes.narration: Real actin and tubulin differ. Each subunit arrives carrying fresh ATP or GTP. Some time after joining, it hydrolyses that nucleotide and releases the phosphate. Those old subunits then hold on less tightly.

scenes.tts: Here is the whole idea. Hydrolysis after joining gives one polymer two kinds of end. A tight end shows fresh subunits and has a low critical concentration. A loose end shows old subunits and has a high one.
scenes.visual: Same filament: a gold tip at the right end, blue (old) blocks exposed at the left end. On 'two kinds of end' the single TEAL tick on the gauge splits into two ticks that slide apart: a low GREEN tick and a high RED tick. On 'A tight end' the right end gets a GREEN tag 'tight' and a line joins it to the low GREEN tick, labelled 'tight Cc'. On 'A loose end' the left end gets a RED tag 'loose' joined to the high RED tick, labelled 'loose Cc'. Gold dots keep docking at the right; blue blocks keep wobbling at the left.
scenes.narration: Here is the whole idea. Hydrolysis after joining gives one polymer two kinds of end. A tight end shows fresh subunits and has a low critical concentration. A loose end shows old subunits and has a high one.

scenes.tts: So set the free subunits between the two levels: above the tight end's, below the loose end's. What can the polymer do now?
scenes.visual: On 'between the two levels' the band on the gauge between the GREEN and RED ticks shades pale TEAL and the pointer slides into it. On 'above the tight end's' the GREEN tick pulses; on 'below the loose end's' the RED tick pulses. On 'What can the polymer do' a question card in TEXT, size 34, appears above the filament: 'Between the levels: what happens?'. Dots keep drifting.
scenes.narration: So set the free subunits between the two levels: above the tight end's, below the loose end's. What can the polymer do now?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause: the question card and the shaded band hold; the pointer bobs gently inside the band; free dots drift slowly. Nothing new is added.

scenes.tts: It cannot come to rest. Actin answers in space. Its barbed end adds subunits fast and stays fresh: a tight end that grows. Its pointed end shows old subunits: a loose end that shrinks. When gain and loss match, the length holds while subunits flow through. That is treadmilling.
scenes.visual: On 'cannot come to rest' the question card fades. On 'Actin answers in space' a TEXT label 'actin filament' appears above; the right end is labelled 'barbed' (GREEN tag 'tight') and the left end 'pointed' (RED tag 'loose'). On 'adds subunits fast' gold blocks dock quickly at the barbed end and the end advances right. On 'a loose end that shrinks' blue blocks drop off the pointed end, which also moves right. One block is outlined in white as it docks at the barbed end. On 'gain and loss match' a fixed-length bracket appears above the filament, labelled 'same length'; both ends advance right at the same speed while the outlined block stays fixed in the world, ages from gold to blue, and is eventually reached by the pointed end and falls off on 'flow through'. On 'treadmilling' the word appears under the filament in TEXT, size 40. Keep the camera fixed so lattice subunits do not appear to slide along the filament.
scenes.narration: It cannot come to rest. Actin answers in space. Its barbed end adds subunits fast and stays fresh: a tight end that grows. Its pointed end shows old subunits: a loose end that shrinks. When gain and loss match, the length holds while subunits flow through. That is treadmilling.

scenes.tts: A microtubule answers in time instead. While growing, it wears a cap of fresh G T P tubulin, so its end stays tight. Behind the cap, G D P tubulin is held straight only by its neighbours.
scenes.caption: A microtubule answers in time instead. While growing, it wears a cap of fresh GTP-tubulin, so its end stays tight. Behind the cap, GDP-tubulin is held straight only by its neighbours.
scenes.visual: On 'A microtubule' the actin filament transforms into the wide tube from the hook (five visible parallel rows of blocks, labelled 'microtubule, schematic'), filling about 60% of frame height, plus end at right, seed off-frame left. The small clock top-right starts running. On 'wears a cap' gold blocks dock at the plus end across all rows and a GOLD bracket labelled 'GTP cap' rides along the tip; the GREEN tag 'tight' sits on the end. The gold-to-blue wave keeps running behind the tip, so the cap stays short while the tube grows. On 'Behind the cap' the blue region is labelled 'GDP lattice'. On 'held straight only by its neighbours' each blue row shows a faint curled ghost of itself, and thin TEXT ties to the rows beside it hold it straight; the ties visibly strain.
scenes.narration: A microtubule answers in time instead. While growing, it wears a cap of fresh GTP-tubulin, so its end stays tight. Behind the cap, GDP-tubulin is held straight only by its neighbours.

scenes.tts: The cap can be lost by chance, or when growth slows and hydrolysis catches up. Then the end turns loose. Its protofilaments peel outward, and it shortens many times faster than it grew. That switch is a catastrophe. Growth starting again is a rescue.
scenes.visual: Same tube. On 'lost by chance' the gold cap flickers and briefly thins while docking continues unchanged; on 'growth slows' docking slows, the gold dots near the tip thin, and the blue front overtakes the gold bracket until it is gone. On 'turns loose' the end tag flips from GREEN 'tight' to RED 'loose'. On 'peel outward' the ties at the tip snap, the rows curl outward like ram's horns, and the tube retreats fast to the left. Bottom strip: a length-versus-time trace labelled 'schematic' draws in step with the tube: a gentle rise during growth, a drop many times steeper during shortening. On 'catastrophe' the top of the drop gets a RED dot labelled 'catastrophe'. On 'rescue' the retreat stops, new gold blocks dock, a GOLD cap re-forms, the tag flips back to GREEN, the trace turns upward, and a GREEN dot labelled 'rescue' marks the turn.
scenes.narration: The cap can be lost by chance, or when growth slows and hydrolysis catches up. Then the end turns loose. Its protofilaments peel outward, and it shortens many times faster than it grew. That switch is a catastrophe. Growth starting again is a rescue.

scenes.tts: Exactly what commits an end to collapse is still argued, and in cells other proteins tune the rates. Hydrolysis gives tight and loose ends, so the polymer cannot simply settle. Cells use that restlessness to search their interior and rebuild.
scenes.visual: On 'what commits an end' a RED '?' tag hangs over the frayed tip of the tube, labelled 'debated'. On 'other proteins' three small TEXT chips 'accessory proteins' slide in beside the tube; one small rate clock speeds up while another slows down. On 'Hydrolysis gives tight' the frame splits: left, the gold crystal cube from the hook sits still, labelled 'settles'; right, the microtubule grows and collapses in a loop above the actin filament treadmilling. On 'cannot simply settle' the GREEN and RED tags flash on both polymers. On 'Cells use that restlessness' zoom out to a simple cell outline (schematic) with a central block and many tubes radiating from it, each growing and collapsing on its own; one tube that touches a small target block at the edge stays, the others keep switching.
scenes.narration: Exactly what commits an end to collapse is still argued, and in cells other proteins tune the rates. Hydrolysis gives tight and loose ends, so the polymer cannot simply settle. Cells use that restlessness to search their interior and rebuild.

scenes.visual: End card (EndCard), LINE: 'Hydrolysis gives tight and loose ends, so the polymer cannot simply settle.' The radiating tubes keep growing and collapsing faintly behind it.
